title: Angular router: routes, links and parameters
goal: Turn your playground into a multi-page app with routes, navigation links and URL parameters.

concepts: Routes array: path, component, redirectTo with pathMatch: 'full', and '**' last
<router-outlet /> and provideRouter(routes)
routerLink and routerLinkActive for navigation
Route parameters (/courses/:id) read as component inputs with withComponentInputBinding()
Query parameters (?level=beginner) and Router.navigate
Order matters: the first matching route wins

resources.title: Angular: Read route state (component input binding)

build.task: In angular-playground, add routing: / (home), /courses (course page), /courses/:id (course detail), /board (task board), /ui (showcase) and a ** not-found page. Add a top nav with routerLink and routerLinkActive highlighting. The course detail page reads id as an input (withComponentInputBinding), finds the course in CourseStore via a computed, and shows 'Course not found' for bad ids. Course filters sync to query params (?q=…&level=…) so a filtered URL can be shared and reloaded.
acceptance: All routes work, including direct URL entry and browser back/forward
Active nav link highlighted with routerLinkActive
/courses/:id reads id as a component input and handles unknown ids
Filters are reflected in query params and restored on reload
** route is last and shows a helpful 404 page with a link home

hints: app.config.ts: provideRouter(routes, withComponentInputBinding()). Then in the detail component: id = input.required<string>(); course = computed(() => this.store.byId(this.id())).
Query params: inject Router and call this.router.navigate([], { queryParams: { q, level }, queryParamsHandling: 'merge' }). Read them back with inputs too (q = input<string>()).
routerLinkActive="font-semibold text-brand-600" plus [routerLinkActiveOptions]="{ exact: true }" on the home link, otherwise '/' is active everywhere.

explainBack.q: How does the id in /courses/42 reach your detail component?
Why must the ** route be last?
lookFor: would hide all routes after it

lastHintExplanation: The router matches the URL against routes in order. /courses/:id captures '42' as the id parameter, and withComponentInputBinding() hands route params (and query params) to component inputs with the same name. ** matches every URL, so it must come last or it will swallow every route below it.

predict.q: Routes: [{ path: 'courses', ... }, { path: 'courses/:id', ... }]. URL: /courses/new. Which route matches?
predict.why: 'courses' only matches the full path /courses; 'courses/:id' matches with id 'new'.

title: Lazy loading, guards and redirects
goal: Split your app into lazily loaded pages and protect routes with guards.

concepts: loadComponent for lazy loading a page
Seeing lazy chunks in the build output and Network tab
Functional guards: CanActivateFn returning true, false or a UrlTree
CanDeactivateFn for 'unsaved changes' warnings
Route data and titles (title: 'Courses')
Child routes and layouts

build.task: In angular-playground: convert every page route to loadComponent and confirm separate chunks with ng build. Add a fake AuthService (signal isLoggedIn, login(), logout()) and a /login page. Protect /board with an authGuard that redirects to /login?returnUrl=/board, and after login navigate back to returnUrl. Add a CanDeactivate guard on a new /board/new page with a form, which asks 'Discard unsaved changes?' if the form is dirty. Give every route a title.
acceptance: All pages lazy-loaded; ng build output lists separate chunks
Visiting /board logged out redirects to /login with returnUrl, then back after login
Leaving /board/new with unsaved changes asks for confirmation; clean form leaves freely
Every route sets the browser tab title
Guards are functional (CanActivateFn / CanDeactivateFn) using inject()

hints: Guard: export const authGuard: CanActivateFn = (_route, state) => inject(AuthService).isLoggedIn() || inject(Router).createUrlTree(['/login'], { queryParams: { returnUrl: state.url } });
CanDeactivate: give the page component a hasUnsavedChanges() method; the guard calls it and returns confirm(...) only if it's true. (Using confirm here is fine for practice.)
proof: Commit with guards and lazy routes; paste the ng build chunk list in the commit message.

explainBack.q: What does lazy loading change for a user opening the home page?
lookFor: page code fetched only when visited

explainBack.q: Walk through your authGuard redirect and how returnUrl brings the user back.
lookFor: login reads returnUrl and navigates there

explainBack.q: Is a client-side guard real security? Why or why not?
lookFor: no, users can change client code
the server must check auth for data

lastHintExplanation: loadComponent splits each page into its own JavaScript chunk that's downloaded only when the route is visited, so the first load is smaller. A guard returning a UrlTree tells the router to redirect, and carrying returnUrl lets login send the user back. Guards are UX, not security: anyone can bypass client code, so the server must protect the data.

predict.q: A CanActivateFn returns false (not a UrlTree) when the user isn't logged in. What happens when they click the link?
options: Navigation is cancelled; they stay where they are
predict.why: false just blocks navigation; a UrlTree redirects.

title: Reactive forms
goal: Build forms with typed reactive form controls and built-in validators.

concepts: Template-driven vs reactive forms (we use reactive)
FormControl, FormGroup, FormArray; FormBuilder with nonNullable
Validators: required, minLength, maxLength, email, pattern, min, max
Binding: [formGroup], formControlName, (ngSubmit)
Form state: valid/invalid, touched/dirty, value vs getRawValue()
Import ReactiveFormsModule in the component

build.task: In angular-playground, build /signup with a reactive form: name (required, 2–50 chars), email (required, email), phone (Indian mobile: pattern ^[6-9]\d{9}$), password (required, min 8), course (select, required), and a FormArray of 'skills' where the user can add and remove skill inputs (at least 1). Disable submit while invalid; on submit, mark all as touched, and if valid show the typed value in a summary card and reset the form. Use FormBuilder.nonNullable so values are typed without null.
acceptance: ReactiveFormsModule imported; form built with fb.nonNullable
All listed validators applied; the phone pattern rejects 5123456789 and 98765
Skills FormArray supports add and remove, with at least one required
Submit button disabled while invalid; ngSubmit used
Summary shows the typed value; form resets afterwards

hints: this.fb.nonNullable.group({ name: ['', [Validators.required, Validators.minLength(2), Validators.maxLength(50)]], ... }). Note the validators go in an array as the second item.
FormArray: skills: this.fb.nonNullable.array([this.fb.nonNullable.control('', Validators.required)]). In the template, loop over skills.controls with @for and use [formControl]="ctrl".
Reading values: this.form.getRawValue() includes disabled controls and is fully typed.

explainBack.q: What's the difference between dirty and touched?
lookFor: touched: field was focused then blurred
used to decide when to show errors

explainBack.q: Why use reactive forms instead of reading inputs manually like in Week 7?

lastHintExplanation: dirty means the user changed the value; touched means the field was focused and then left. Showing errors only once a field is touched (or after submit) avoids yelling at users before they've typed. Reactive forms keep the whole form model, its validation and its state in typed TypeScript, which is easier to test and extend than reading the DOM manually.

predict.q: fb.group({ age: [null as number | null, Validators.min(18)] }); the user leaves age empty. Is the control valid?
predict.why: min only checks values that are present; add required to forbid empty.

title: Validation messages and custom validators
goal: Show clear validation messages and write your own field and cross-field validators.

concepts: Reading errors: control.hasError('required'), control.errors
When to show errors: touched or submitted
Custom validator function: (control) => ValidationErrors | null
Cross-field validators on the FormGroup (password match, date range)
Async validators (e.g. 'username taken') with a debounce
A reusable field-error component

build.task: Improve /signup: add confirmPassword with a group-level passwordsMatch validator; a custom strongPassword validator (upper, lower, digit, 8+) that reports which rules are missing; a noWhitespace validator for name; and an async usernameAvailable validator that checks against a fake list after a 400 ms delay (show 'Checking…'). Build a reusable field-error component that takes a control and a map of messages and shows the right message only when touched or after submit. Write unit tests for the 3 sync validators.
acceptance: passwordsMatch is applied to the FormGroup and shows the error under confirm password
strongPassword returns which rules failed, and the UI lists them
Async username check shows 'Checking…' and an error for taken names
field-error component reused for every field; errors appear only after touch/submit
Validator unit tests pass (ng test)

hints: Sync validator: export function noWhitespace(c: AbstractControl): ValidationErrors | null { return c.value?.trim() ? null : { whitespace: true }; }
Group validator: this.fb.group({...}, { validators: passwordsMatch }); inside, read group.get('password')?.value and group.get('confirmPassword')?.value.
Async validator: return (c) => timer(400).pipe(map(() => taken.includes(c.value) ? { taken: true } : null)). The control's status is 'PENDING' while it runs.
proof: Commit with validators, field-error component and tests.

explainBack.q: Why does passwordsMatch go on the group instead of on one control?
lookFor: a control validator only sees its own value

explainBack.q: What does your validator return when the value is valid, and why?
lookFor: Angular treats null as no errors

lastHintExplanation: A validator returns null when the value is valid, or an object of error keys (with optional details) when it isn't. A control-level validator only sees its own value, so a rule comparing two fields (password and confirm) belongs on the parent FormGroup, which re-validates when either field changes.

predict.q: A validator function returns {} (an empty object) for a valid value. What does Angular think?
options: Invalid, because errors is a non-null object
predict.why: Angular treats any non-null result as errors; return null for valid.

title: Project: a notes app with routing and forms
goal: Combine routing, forms, services and signals into a complete multi-page notes app.

concepts: Feature planning: routes, components, store, forms
Create and edit sharing one form component
Navigating after save; showing a toast message
Unsaved-changes guard on the editor
Search, tags and sort with computed signals

build.task: Create a NEW repo angular-notes (Angular + Tailwind). Routes: /notes (list with search, tag filter and sort), /notes/new and /notes/:id/edit (the same NoteEditor component in create or edit mode), /notes/:id (detail with rendered tags, created/updated dates, delete with confirmation modal) and **. A NotesStore (signals) persists to localStorage. The editor uses a reactive form (title required 3–100, body required, tags as comma-separated input converted to an array, pinned checkbox), a CanDeactivate guard, and shows a toast after saving. Pinned notes appear first.
acceptance: All routes work with direct URLs and back/forward
One editor component handles create and edit (pre-filled in edit mode)
Search, tag filter and sort combine; pinned notes always first
Unsaved changes prompt when leaving a dirty editor
Delete asks for confirmation using your ui-modal
Data persists; README explains features and how to run

hints: Editor mode: id = input<string>(); isEdit = computed(() => !!this.id()). In the constructor or an effect, if editing, patchValue the form with the existing note (once).
Tags: 'angular, forms, ' → value.split(',').map(t => t.trim()).filter(Boolean). Store them lowercase to make filtering easy.
Toast: a small ToastService with a messages signal and show(text) that removes the message after 3 seconds; render it once in the app component.

explainBack.q: How does one NoteEditor component know whether it's creating or editing?
lookFor: route param id present or not

explainBack.q: Explain how your pinned-first sort works together with the user's chosen sort.
lookFor: sort by pinned first then by chosen key

lastHintExplanation: The editor knows its mode from the route: /notes/new has no id and /notes/:id/edit does. With input binding, id() is undefined or a string, and isEdit is computed from it. In edit mode the form is patched once with the note's values, and save calls update instead of add. A two-level sort compares pinned first and falls back to the chosen key.

predict.why: trim turns ' ' into '', and filter(Boolean) removes empty strings.

dsa.note: Two stacks make a queue: one for input, one for output.

hints: Every URL shows not-found: what does the router do with the first route that matches?
The redirect throws an error in the console about pathMatch. Read it: an empty path matches every URL as a prefix.

For the form, read the template errors in the console one by one. One is about binding to formGroup (what must the component import?), one is about a control name. Also: what's the third item in a FormBuilder control array?

explainBack.q: List the 5 bugs and the exact error or symptom that led you to each.
lookFor: ReactiveFormsModule not imported → can't bind to formGroup
minLength passed as async validator → must be in an array

explainBack.q: Why does an empty-path redirect need pathMatch: 'full'?
lookFor: '' is a prefix of every URL

lastHintExplanation: 1) '**' first matches every URL, so move it last. 2) path '' with prefix matching would match every URL, so Angular requires pathMatch: 'full' on that redirect. 3) [formGroup] only exists with ReactiveFormsModule in the component's imports. 4) formControlName="tittle" doesn't match the control 'title'. 5) In ['', a, b], the third item is the async validators slot, so wrap sync validators in one array: ['', [Validators.required, Validators.minLength(3)]].

predict.q: fb.control('', Validators.required, Validators.minLength(3)). What is minLength used as?
predict.why: The third argument is for async validators.
